subtitle: When Words Became Power in the Court of Kannauj

panels.shot: wide, ceremonial court tableau with Kannauj’s palace rising over the Ganga plains
panels.action: Rajashekhara stands before a royal audience in Mahendrapala’s Kannauj, manuscript in hand, while Avantisundari sits beside him on a low jewel-studded seat, calm and learned, as courtiers lean in around them.

dialogue.text: In Mahendrapala’s Kannauj, Rajashekhara dared to build a court of poets—and to name Avantisundari, his wife, as his learned equal. How did words become the empire’s subtlest power?

i18n.hi: महेन्द्रपाल के कन्नौज में राजशेखर ने साहस किया – कवियों का दरबार रचा, और अपनी पत्नी अवन्तीसुन्दरी को अपना विद्वान साथी घोषित किया। शब्द कैसे बने साम्राज्य की सबसे सूक्ष्म ताकत?

panels.shot: slow push-in from river to city, showing urban bustle beneath royal terraces
panels.action: The sun rises over the Ganga near Kannauj, boats glide on the river, and the great city’s temples and palaces catch the light while scholars and traders move through its streets.

dialogue.text: Around 900 CE, Kannauj was more than a capital. Under Mahendrapala I, the Gurjara-Pratihara court sought to rule not only with armies, but with language and learning.

i18n.hi: लगभग ९०० ईस्वी में कन्नौज सिर्फ राजधानी नहीं था। महेन्द्रपाल प्रथम के राज में गुर्जर-प्रतिहार दरबार फौजों से ही नहीं, भाषा और विद्या से भी राज करना चाहता था।

panels.shot: interior wide of court hall with the king enthroned and scholars gathered
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall, Mahendrapala sits on a high throne, ministers at his side, while a circle of poets and pandits debate animatedly before him, palm-leaf manuscripts stacked nearby.

dialogue.text: Mahendrapala inherited Bhoja’s legacy of patronage. Kannauj drew thinkers from across the north, becoming a node in the Sanskrit cosmopolis—a world where polished verse signaled royal greatness.

i18n.hi: महेन्द्रपाल ने भोज की सरपरस्ती की विरासत संभाली। कन्नौज उत्तर से विद्वानों को खींच लाया, संस्कृत जगत का एक केन्द्रीय केंद्र बना – जहाँ निखरी कविता से राजवैभव झलकता था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Rajashekhara among other poets, slightly off-center
panels.action: Rajashekhara sits among other court poets, older and younger, his face thoughtful as he listens, fingers resting on a manuscript, while others recite verses in ornate Sanskrit.

dialogue.text: Among these poets was Rajashekhara. Not just a maker of praise poems, he began to ask a harder question: what makes a true poet—and what kind of learning should a court really honor?

i18n.hi: इन कवियों में थे राजशेखर। वे सिर्फ प्रशस्ति लिखने वाले नहीं थे; वे कठिन सवाल पूछने लगे – सच्चा कवि किसे कहें, और दरबार किस तरह की विद्या को सम्मान दे?

panels.shot: intimate interior, Rajashekhara and Avantisundari seated together at night
panels.action: In a quieter chamber lit by oil lamps, Rajashekhara sits cross-legged, writing on a palm leaf, while Avantisundari leans close, pointing at a line as they discuss and share a manuscript spread before them.

dialogue.text: His own works name Avantisundari, his wife, as his companion in thought. In his prefaces, he acknowledges her counsel—an unusual glimpse of a learned woman within elite literary life.

i18n.hi: अपने ग्रंथों में वे अपनी पत्नी अवन्तीसुन्दरी को विचार–सहचरी कहते हैं। प्रस्तावनाओं में वे उसकी सलाह मानते हैं – उच्च साहित्यिक जगत में एक विदुषी स्त्री की अनोखी झलक।

panels.shot: close-up on a manuscript leaf titled “Kavyamimamsa” being unrolled
panels.action: Hands carefully unroll a palm-leaf manuscript whose opening verse is being traced by Rajashekhara’s stylus, Avantisundari watching with focused attention beside him.

dialogue.text: In his Kavyamimamsa, Rajashekhara did something bold. He did not just compose poetry; he set out the first full guide in Sanskrit to how poets should be educated, and what poetry could do for power.

i18n.hi: अपनी ‘काव्यमीमांसा’ में राजशेखर ने साहसी काम किया। वे केवल कविता नहीं रचे; उन्होंने पहली पूरी संस्कृत मार्गदर्शिका लिखी – कवि कैसे शिक्षित हों, और कविता सत्ता के लिए क्या कर सके।

panels.shot: conceptual montage: faint overlays of grammar charts, musical instruments, maps
panels.action: Around the seated couple, faint symbolic images appear—grammatical diagrams, a veena, a celestial chart, a map-like outline of regions—suggesting the breadth of knowledge they discuss.

dialogue.text: Kavyamimamsa lists the poet’s training: grammar, metrics, music, sciences, politics, and social customs. For Rajashekhara, a poet had to know the world—so his verse could address it fully.

i18n.hi: काव्यमीमांसा में कवि की शिक्षा गिनाई है – व्याकरण, छन्द, संगीत, विज्ञान, राजनीति, और लोकाचार। राजशेखर के लिए कवि को जगत जानना था – तभी उसका काव्य उसे भरपूर छू सके।

panels.shot: wide map-like visualization of the subcontinent with lines radiating from Kannauj
panels.action: A stylized view of the Indian subcontinent appears, with scripted place-names and lines of light radiating out from Kannauj to distant regions, evoking the imagined geography of his text.

dialogue.text: He scattered place-names from many regions through his works. Pollock notes how such geography map the Sanskrit cosmopolis—a world bound not by one state, but by a shared literary language.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने अपने ग्रंथों में कई प्रदेशों के नाम बिखेर दिए। पोलॉक बताते हैं, यही भूगोल संस्कृत जगत का नक्शा बनाता है – एक संसार, जो किसी एक राज्य से नहीं, साझा भाषा से बँधा है।

panels.shot: medium shot in court, Rajashekhara reciting, king and courtiers listening keenly
panels.action: In the royal hall, Rajashekhara stands poised, reciting from his theoretical text, while Mahendrapala leans forward, and a circle of court poets listen with mixed curiosity and respect.

dialogue.text: “A king’s glory,” he says, “shines in the poets he fosters.”

i18n.hi: “राजा की कीर्ति,” वे कहते हैं, “उन्हीं कवियों में चमकती है, जिन्हें वह पालता है।”

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Mahendrapala considering, with scholars in the background
panels.action: Mahendrapala rests his chin on his hand, looking out over the assembly of scholars and scribes, while attendants hold ornate manuscripts behind him to suggest a culture of letters.

dialogue.text: Mahendrapala’s support made Kannauj a literary center. Through poets like Rajashekhara, his court joined a larger competition: who could most convincingly claim to rule the world of culture?

i18n.hi: महेन्द्रपाल के सहारे कन्नौज साहित्य–केन्द्र बना। राजशेखर जैसे कवियों के जरिये उसका दरबार बड़ी होड़ में कूदा – कौन सबसे दमदार ढंग से संस्कृति–जगत पर अपना हक जताए?

panels.shot: dramatic theater interior with a small royal audience watching a stage
panels.action: In an intimate performance hall, lamps light a raised stage where actors prepare to perform, while Rajashekhara and Avantisundari sit together in the front row, observing intently.

dialogue.text: Not all his work was in high Sanskrit. His play Karpuramanjari, in a mix of Sanskrit and a Prakrit, brought courtly themes into more accessible speech, revealing another dimension of his craft.

i18n.hi: उनकी सारी रचना ऊँची संस्कृत में नहीं थी। ‘कर्पूरमञ्जरी’ नाटक, संस्कृत और प्राकृत के मेल में, दरबारी विषयों को सरल बोल में लाया – उनके शिल्प का नया रूप दिखा।

panels.shot: close-up of Avantisundari’s face as she reacts thoughtfully to the play
panels.action: Avantisundari watches the stage, her expression alert and reflective, turning slightly toward Rajashekhara as if to share an insight about the unfolding scene.

dialogue.text: In his introductions, Rajashekhara credits Avantisundari’s opinions on his compositions. The record does not preserve her own writings, but his words place her firmly within his circle of learning.

i18n.hi: भूमिकाओं में राजशेखर अपनी रचनाओं पर अवन्तीसुन्दरी के मतों का श्रेय देते हैं। उसकी खुद की रचनाएँ नहीं बचीं, पर उसके शब्द उसे उनके विद्या–वृत्त में मजबूती से बैठा देते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of the couple debating over a manuscript, gentle but intense
panels.action: Seated across from each other, Rajashekhara gestures toward a passage, while Avantisundari replies with calm firmness, one hand resting on the text between them in a moment of shared reasoning.

dialogue.speaker: Avantisundari
dialogue.text: “Then teach, not only praise. Tell them what a poet must know.”

i18n.hi: “तो सिखाओ, सिर्फ प्रशंसा मत करो। बताओ, कवि को क्या–क्या जानना चाहिए।”

panels.shot: symbolic overhead shot of the court library, scrolls arranged in rows
panels.action: Rows of neatly stacked palm-leaf bundles and bound manuscripts fill shelves in a court library, with faint silhouettes of scribes copying texts in the aisles below.

dialogue.text: Kavyamimamsa moves from definitions of poetry to the craft of composition and the social roles of poets. It was a handbook for shaping minds—within a court that knew minds were part of its power.

i18n.hi: काव्यमीमांसा कविता की परिभाषा से चलकर रचना–कला और कवियों की सामाजिक भूमिकाओं तक पहुँचती है। यह मन गढ़ने की किताब थी – उस दरबार के लिए, जो जानता था कि मन भी उसकी शक्ति है।

panels.shot: conceptual split-screen: on one side warriors and banners; on the other poets
panels.action: On one side, warriors stand with spears and banners before city walls; on the other, poets and scholars sit reciting and writing, the two worlds balanced in the same visual frame.

dialogue.text: Pollock reads courts like Mahendrapala’s as sites of ‘soft power’: conquest through prestige, style, and shared Sanskrit. Rajashekhara’s theory helped define how that power of words was to be trained.

i18n.hi: पोलॉक महेन्द्रपाल जैसे दरबारों को ‘नरम शक्ति’ की जगह मानते हैं – प्रतिष्ठा, शैली और साझा संस्कृत से की गई विजय। राजशेखर की सिद्धि ने बताया, इस शब्द–शक्ति को कैसे साधें।

panels.shot: medium shot of Rajashekhara teaching younger poets, Avantisundari nearby
panels.action: Rajashekhara addresses a small group of younger poets seated before him, explaining with his hand raised, while Avantisundari sits at the side, listening, her presence acknowledged but relaxed.

dialogue.text: We do not know every detail of his teaching. But through his text, we see the ideal: a court where poets studied grammar and governance, music and society—rather than merely flattering their patron.

i18n.hi: हम उनकी शिक्षा के हर ब्योरे को नहीं जानते। पर उनके ग्रंथ से आदर्श दिखता है – ऐसा दरबार, जहाँ कवि व्याकरण और शासन, संगीत और समाज पढ़ते हैं, सिर्फ अपने पालक की चापलूसी नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up of Kavyamimamsa manuscript being copied by a scribe
panels.action: A court scribe carefully inscribes the verses of Kavyamimamsa on a fresh palm leaf, while the older original lies beside it, slightly worn from use.

dialogue.text: Kavyamimamsa and Karpuramanjari survived in manuscripts through centuries of copying. They now stand as rare windows into how one poet at Kannauj thought about creativity and education.

i18n.hi: काव्यमीमांसा और कर्पूरमञ्जरी सदियों तक पाण्डुलिपियों में नकल होती रहीं। आज वे कन्नौज के एक कवि की रचना–दृष्टि और शिक्षा–विचार को देखने की दुर्लभ खिड़कियाँ हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot pulling back from the court into the sky, city shrinking below
panels.action: The view rises above Kannauj’s roofs, the royal hall and river growing small below, as tiny figures of the couple fade into the grand sweep of the land and sky.

dialogue.text: Empires shift, and Kannauj’s political power waned. But Rajashekhara’s insistence that a poet must know many disciplines—and his naming of Avantisundari as partner in that learning—still reach us.

i18n.hi: साम्राज्य बदलते हैं, कन्नौज की राज–शक्ति घट गई। पर राजशेखर का आग्रह कि कवि बहु–विद्याओं का ज्ञाता हो, और उनकी साथी अवन्तीसुन्दरी का नाम विद्या–सहभागी के रूप में लेना – आज भी हम तक आता है।

panels.shot: quiet interior, a modern scholar reading Kavyamimamsa with ghostly overlay of the couple
panels.action: A present-day scholar sits at a desk with an edited volume of Kavyamimamsa open, while faint, translucent figures of Rajashekhara and Avantisundari appear above the pages as if remembered through the text.

dialogue.text: Their story reminds us that a court—or any institution—shines brightest when learning is shared, and when power asks not only for praise, but for minds trained to understand the world together.

i18n.hi: उनकी कहानी दिखाती है कि दरबार या कोई भी संस्था तभी सबसे ज्यादा जगमगाती है, जब विद्या बाँटी जाए – और सत्ता सिर्फ प्रशंसा न माँगे, बल्कि ऐसे मनों को, जो मिलकर संसार को समझना चाहें।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Words Became Power in the Court of Kannauj
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब शब्द बने शक्ति, कन्नौज के दरबार में
